newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait share index down, fears of a correction.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait share index down, fears of a correction.

text.p: Fear of a correction is expected to depress liquidity on the Kuwait Stock Exchange on Monday after the index dropped 31.5 points to 1,888.6 the previous day.
"There are stronger fears of a correction and investors are waiting to see lower prices before going back in again," leading economist Jassim al-Saadoun said.

Although the value of shares traded on Sunday rose to 23 million dinars ($77 million) from 20 million dinars the previous day it was slightly less than half of the daily average for the week ending on Wednesday.
Market analysts expect traded value to stay within the 20-30 million dinar range on Monday with fewer investors going into the market to buy shares.

"I think it is now a matter of when the correction will happen and not if a correction will happen," added Saadoun who stressed that the sooner the correction occured the less the losses were likely to be.
The drop in recent days "is not the real correction it is a partial one," he added.

The index eased 1.76 percent to 1919.9 last week after a long upward trend set new records in recent weeks. It rose 218.4 points in October month-on-month to 1,954.2 -- a 43 percent increase from January 2.
Traded volume reached 74 million dinars on Sunday compared to 71.6 million the previous day and a daily average of 180 million shares the previous week.
Out of 45 concenrs traded on Sunday, shares of three companies rose, 35 dropped and seven were non-movers.
The Kuwait market is open for 2-1/2 hours from Saturday to Wednesday.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest through mutual funds.
